s0.text: What are [[LLMs]] and how do they [[work]]?

s1.text: LLMs are essentially built to do one thing: [[predict the next word]].

s2.text: LLMs are essentially built to do one thing: predict the next word, after any piece of text -- or prompt -- that is fed into them.

s2b.text: LLMs are essentially built to do one thing: predict the next word, after any piece of text -- or prompt -- that is fed into them.

s3.text: LLMs are built through intensive [[training on huge corpora of text]] (billions of words).

s4.text: LLMs are built through intensive training on huge corpora of text (billions of words). During training, they pick up statistical regularities and learn what the next word might be.

s5.text: [[Decoder-style]] LLMs (such as GPT) are [[generative]] machines. They sample [[the next word]] from a [[computed list of the most likely ones]].

s5b.text: Decoder-style LLMs (such as GPT) are generative machines. They sample the next word from a computed list of the most likely ones, then the one-word-longer sequence is fed back and the process is repeated.

s5c.text: Decoder-style LLMs (such as GPT) are generative machines. They sample the next word from a computed list of the most likely ones, then the one-word-longer sequence is fed back and the process is repeated, progressively generating a block of text.

s6.text: Decoder-style LLMs (such as GPT) are generative machines. They sample the next token from a computed list of the most likely ones, then the one-token-longer sequence is fed back and the process is repeated, progressively generating a block of text.

s7.text: Decoder-style LLMs (such as GPT) are essentially [[sequential next-token producers]].

s8.text: Behind this apparent fluency sit a handful of ideas worth unpacking: [[tokenization]] and [[embedding]] (turning text into numbers), [[attention]] (weighing context), and the [[transformer architecture]] that ties them together.

s9.text: Start with [[embedding]]: each token becomes a point in a high-dimensional space, where distance stands in for meaning.

s10.text: Project the space down to 2D and clusters emerge. [[Animal words]] land near each other -- cat, dog, fish, bird.

s11.text: [[Action verbs]] carve out their own region -- predict, simulate, compute, estimate.

s12.text: [[Statistical terms]] cluster elsewhere -- probability, variance, posterior, distribution.

s13.text: Even [[abstract categories]] separate cleanly: king, queen, prince, princess.
